key_insight: Neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group oxides are largely captured by two bulk descriptors: crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: The model can help screen oxide materials for vacancy-dependent energy applications without explicit defect calculations, though solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Surveyed 39 binary oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to identify reconstructed defect ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using pristine-bulk properties.
evidence_signal: Formation energies spanned 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieved a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: Predictions require caution when vacancy electrons are accommodated through mechanisms other than cation reduction.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
